title: Converting and changing the category are recorded in the Audit Log
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, in status Approved.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Open the work order's three-dots menu.
  3. Click "Convert to No Charge".
  4. Pick "Goodwill" in Category.
  5. Click the confirming Convert to No Charge button.
  6. Open the work order's three-dots menu.
  7. Click "Change category".
  8. Pick "Comeback" in Category.
  9. Click Save.
  10. Open the work order's Audit Log.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The menu shows "Convert to No Charge".

Step 3:

  • The confirmation opens.

Step 4:

  • Goodwill is picked.

Step 5:

  • The "No Charge" badge shows.

Step 6:

  • The menu shows "Change category".

Step 7:

  • The window opens.

Step 8:

  • Comeback is picked.

Step 9:

  • The window closes.

Step 10:

  • The Audit Log has a row for Convert to No Charge and a row for Change category, each with the user and the time.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close)

  • S2-R13: “The classification is written on the work order when it is created, when its customer changes and when it is converted; the closed record carries it too, with the category. Lists, reports and integrations read it from there, never from the customer flag. Converting to no charge or to billable, changing the category, a shop supplies amount change, Make internal (S1-R11, on each work order), Close with its posting date, Reopen, and adding or removing a customer's Internal flag are recorded in the work order or customer Audit Log with the user and the time.”
  • S2-R18: “Every classification change writes a read-only system note on the work order (Notes tab, author ShopView, with the user and the time) and an Audit Log row: Convert to No Charge ("Converted to No Charge by [user]. Category [name], original work order [number]. Prices, fees and discounts removed; costs and hours kept."), Change category (from, to, original work order kept or cleared), Convert to Billable ("Every line priced as a new line would be today. Category [name] removed."), Close (posting date, account), Reopen, and the line actions of Story 12 (S12-R6). Work order numbers in notes are links.”
